title: Hotfix: burst signal misdetection causing reserved-pool shortfalls and delayed autoscale
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers experienced degraded throughput and intermittent 503s during a cross-region traffic burst. Root cause analysis indicates the dedicated autoscaler misdetected burst signals when multiple tenants requested short, high-concurrency spikes. The misdetection deferred scale-out decisions due to a time-windowed estimator that undercounted transient qps peaks and a headroom accounting bug that double-counted KV cache occupancy. This ticket tracks the emergency mitigation, code hotfix, rollout plan, and customer communications.
comments: 2026-03-07 02:18 UTC — Incident raised by SRE on-call after PagerDuty alerts: sustained queue growth in reserved pools for region-us-west-2; observed customer escalations from Acme Health and Finlytics. Initial mitigation: increase soft burst limits for affected reserved pools and enable emergency-rebalance to borrow idle GPUs from lower-priority tenants. (Action: SRE team)

2026-03-07 03:05 UTC — Triage call with Eng, SRE, PM and Solutions. Hypothesis: autoscaler estimator uses an EWMA over 60s window which smoothed out sub-60s bursts. Combined with a race between pool-replenish loop and KV cache reconciliation, scale-out was delayed by ~30–45s causing queueing. Agreed to: 1) implement immediate config change to reduce smoothing window to 10s for burst-prone tiers; 2) push a code hotpatch to fix headroom double-count bug; 3) prepare customer comms and status page update.

2026-03-07 05:40 UTC — Hotpatch PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1289 — 'autoscaler: fix headroom double-count + reduce EWMA window for burst tiers'. Hotpatch includes: (a) correct KV cache occupancy accounting by removing legacy double-subtraction; (b) expose smoothing_window as runtime-config with per-tenant override; (c) add emergency scaling bypass flag for on-call to force immediate scale-out. Tests: unit coverage + synthetic load test showing median scale latency from 48s -> 9s under 95th percentile bursts.

2026-03-07 08:20 UTC — Deployed hotpatch to canary reserved pool in us-west-2 (5% of fleet). Observed immediate improvement: queues drained within 12s during a synthetic 2k rps 20s spike. No regressions in memory/KVS metrics. Rolling canary planned across Dedicated clusters over next 2 hours.

2026-03-07 10:45 UTC — Customer comms drafted by PM (Jules Nguyen) and Solutions: message templates for affected customers: root cause, mitigation steps taken, ETA for full rollout, and offer cadence for follow-up postmortem. Sent to Acme Health and Finlytics with apology and next steps. Marked support tickets for SLA credit review.

2026-03-08 01:33 UTC — Full rollout completed across Dedicated clusters; emergency scaling bypass toggled off after verification. Metrics: mean scale latency reduced from 43s -> 11s for burst events; dropped 503s for impacted tenants to <0.01% in the 24h after rollout. Dashboard: internal link to grafana/dashboard?orgId=1&panelId=72 (synthetic burst experiment results).

2026-03-08 04:00 UTC — Post-deploy monitoring: discovered edge case where smoothing_window=10s causes noisy oscillation for very low-QPS tenants with infrequent bursts. Mitigation: introduce per-tenant tier mapping (burst-tier, steady-tier) with default 10s for burst-tier only; update runtime-config docs. (Action: Marco Li + Runtime team)

2026-03-09 09:10 UTC — Retrospective notes: trade-offs considered: shorter EWMA reduces detection latency but risks oscillation; alternative considered was event-driven burst detectors based on token-queue slippage and derivative-of-QPS but higher engineering cost. Chosen short-term approach: config-driven EWMA + headroom fix + plan to implement event-driven detector in Q2. Added task ENG-41990 to roadmap.

2026-03-09 15:22 UTC — Follow-up customer outreach completed. Customers accepted post-incident summary and asked for additional telemetry for their tenants (per-tenant burst histograms). Added to backlog as PM-582. Support offered one month of usage credit to affected customers (following SLA policy).

2026-03-10 11:45 UTC — Documentation updated: runtime-1.21 release notes include autoscaler behavior changes, new runtime-config flags, and guidance for customers to opt-in to burst-tier for latency-sensitive workloads. (Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/8213)

2026-03-10 13:30 UTC — Next steps: 1) harden event-driven burst detector (ENG-41990); 2) implement per-tenant headroom audit and nightly reconciliation job (ENG-42012); 3) create automated chaos test for transient multi-tenant spikes in staging with SLO guardrails (ENG-42108). Assigned owners listed in tickets.
